note: Fc-enhanced CD19 antibodies killed patient CLL cells ex vivo yet inebilizumab did not beat rituximab; CD19 CAR-T expanded and met a CR endpoint as xenografts foretold, at lower CR rates.
label: CLL/SLL (CD19 depleters)

engagement.model: Patient CLL cells with NK effectors (ex-vivo ADCC)
engagement.note: Tafasitamab (XmAb5574) killed patient CLL cells by NK-mediated ADCC more potently than rituximab; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: Potent NK ADCC on patient CLL cells
engagement.quote: XmAb5574 mediates significantly higher ADCC compared with both the humanized anti-CD19 nonengineered antibody it is derived from and also rituximab
engagement.judgement: Opening entry; first public December 2009 (epub), print 2010.

engagement.magnitude_basis: fraction of patients with falling blood/nodal CLL burden against ex-vivo CLL-cell killing
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; NCT01161511 has no posted results (first posted 2010-07-13).
engagement.model: Patient CLL cells with NK effectors (ex-vivo ADCC)
engagement.note: In the first-in-human CLL trial, tafasitamab cleared circulating disease: 66.7% responded by examination and laboratory criteria.
engagement.short: Blood CLL burden fell on tafasitamab
engagement.quote: XmAb5574 showed preliminary efficacy, with 18 patients (66.7%) responding by physical examination criteria and laboratory studies, and 8 patients (29.6%) responding by computed tomography criteria.
engagement.reason: CLL cells cleared as ADCC predicted
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: the ADCC assay's readout (CLL-cell killing) is read against clearance of circulating CLL cells in patients, scored as proximal. Paired by me; the trial paper does not restate the ex-vivo data in its abstract. CT responses (29.6%) were fewer than laboratory responses, so magnitude is direction only.

engagement.model: CD19 CAR-T in immunodeficient-mouse CD19+ leukemia xenografts
engagement.note: Anti-CD19 CARs with 4-1BB persisted >6 months and cleared primary pre-B ALL in immunodeficient mice.
engagement.short: 4-1BB CAR persisted, cleared leukemia in mice
engagement.quote: human T cells expressing anti-CD19 CARs containing CD137 exhibited the greatest antileukemic efficacy and prolonged (>6 months) survival in vivo
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the xenograft track; the xenograft carried ALL, not CLL, cells, the system the CLL trials were built on.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CAR-T persistence (>6 months in mice vs 6 months in blood and marrow) and CD19+ cell loss
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; single patient. NCT01029366 first posted 2009-12-10, results posted 2017-02-28.
engagement.model: CD19 CAR-T in immunodeficient-mouse CD19+ leukemia xenografts
engagement.note: CTL019 expanded >1000-fold in a CLL patient, persisted 6 months and removed CD19+ normal and leukemic B cells, as the mice predicted.
engagement.short: CAR-T expanded, persisted, cleared CD19+ cells
engagement.quote: Engineered cells persisted at high levels for 6 months in the blood and bone marrow and continued to express the chimeric antigen receptor.
engagement.reason: Persistence and B-cell loss as in mice
engagement.judgement: CAR-T expansion and persistence are read as the transgene product (proximal). Paired by me: Porter 2011 does not state the mouse data in its abstract. n=1 at the date of the entry; later CLL cohorts (Porter 2015, Siddiqi 2023) confirmed expansion in most patients.

engagement.model: CAR-T plus concurrent ibrutinib in CLL/ALL xenografts
engagement.note: Concurrent ibrutinib improved CTL019 engraftment, tumor clearance and survival in ALL and CLL xenografts.
engagement.short: Ibrutinib boosted CAR-T engraftment in mice
engagement.quote: ibrutinib exposure does not impair CAR T-cell function in vitro but does improve CAR T-cell engraftment, tumor clearance, and survival in human xenograft models of resistant acute lymphocytic leukemia and CLL
engagement.judgement: Opening entry; a separate track because the system is the xenograft dosed with CAR-T plus ibrutinib, making its own prediction.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CAR-T expansion with vs without concurrent ibrutinib
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Non-randomised comparison with an earlier cohort of the same trial (NCT01865617, first posted 2013-05-31, results posted 2022-05-25). Product JCAR014, a CD19 CAR-T, not the CTL019 dosed in the mice.
engagement.model: CAR-T plus concurrent ibrutinib in CLL/ALL xenografts
engagement.note: With concurrent ibrutinib, CAR-T expansion in CLL patients was equivalent to that without it; CRS was milder.
engagement.short: Ibrutinib did not raise CAR-T expansion
engagement.quote: Compared with CLL patients treated with CAR T cells without ibrutinib, CAR T cells with concurrent ibrutinib were associated with lower CRS severity and lower serum concentrations of CRS-associated cytokines, despite equivalent in vivo CAR T-cell expansion.
engagement.reason: Expansion equal with and without ibrutinib
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: the paper names the preclinical rationale and then reports the comparison, so comparison_stated is true. The xenograft predicted better engraftment; patients showed equivalent expansion, scored contra. Magnitude 'opposite' is used for no effect where an increase was predicted. Fraietta's own three ibrutinib-pretreated patients (prior, not concurrent, ibrutinib) had better expansion, which is a different regimen.

engagement.quote: as well as blood and tissue B cells in human CD19/CD20 double transgenic (Tg) mice at lower concentrations than that of the positive control mAb rituximab.
engagement.note: MEDI-551 out-depleted rituximab in huCD19/CD20 Tg mice; CLL trials posted no B-cell counts to compare.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT00983619 (CLL, DLBCL, FL, MM; results posted 2020-05-13) listed serum B-cell counts but states 'It was pre-specified that B-cell analysis was not required, due to limited data availability.' NCT01466153 lists no B-cell outcome.
engagement.judgement: B-cell depletion, the mouse's readout, was never reported in dosed CLL patients; untested, not_measured.
engagement.model: Human CD19/CD20 transgenic mice (MEDI-551 vs rituximab)

dose.confidence_note: Year 2010 is a proxy for the toxicology package that supported NCT01161511.
dose.note: Tafasitamab was tolerated to 100 mg/kg weekly in monkeys before first-in-human dosing; the data were not public.
dose.quote: tafasitamab was well tolerated after weekly IV administration to cynomolgus monkeys at doses up to 100 mg/kg for 13 weeks, with no target organ toxicities or mortalities.
dose.judgement: Opening proxy dated to first-in-human CLL dosing (2010); the margin was public only in the 2020 review.

dose.magnitude_basis: NOAEL exposure multiple (8-9x) against tolerated 12 mg/kg in CLL
dose.confidence_note: Patient side is Woyach 2014 (abstract: 'No maximal tolerated dose was reached'). The review's human comparator is the DLBCL 12 mg/kg regimen, the same dose as the top CLL cohort.
dose.note: Monkey NOAEL exposures sat 8-9-fold above human; CLL patients were dosed to 12 mg/kg without reaching an MTD.
dose.short: Margin held: no MTD up to 12 mg/kg
dose.quote: Exposure values (AUC and Cmax) at NOAEL (100mg/kg) were 8-9 fold higher than corresponding values in humans.
dose.reason: Stated margin held in CLL patients
dose.judgement: Judgement call: dated 2020, when the margin became public; the patient half (Woyach 2014) was public earlier. The model stated no efficacious exposure target, only the tolerability margin, so only the margin half is scored.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no human-dose statement found in the model papers read.
dose.model: CD19 CAR-T in immunodeficient-mouse CD19+ leukemia xenografts
dose.note: Mouse CAR-T cell numbers do not scale to a human dose; CLL doses (1.5e5/kg CTL019; 50-100e6 liso-cel) came from clinical escalation.
dose.short: Mouse doses gave no human dose
dose.quote: In an immunodeficient mouse xenograft model of primary human pre-B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, human T cells expressing anti-CD19 CARs containing CD137 exhibited the greatest antileukemic efficacy
dose.reason: No human dose stated by the model
dose.judgement: Xenograft doses are cells per mouse with no exposure or occupancy target, so the dose cell stays untested (no_prediction).

efficacy.model: Patient CLL cells with NK effectors (ex-vivo ADCC)
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo ADCC on patient CLL cells ranked Fc-enhanced CD19 antibodies above rituximab.
efficacy.short: Fc-enhanced anti-CD19 beat rituximab ex vivo
efficacy.quote: These findings provide strong support for further clinical development of XmAb5574 as both a monotherapy and in combination with lenalidomide for the therapy of CLL
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The tafasitamab CLL trials (NCT01161511, COSMOS NCT02639910) had safety primary endpoints, so they do not score efficacy.

efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results only (posted 2017-05-31); no journal publication found. The quote defines the primary endpoint; the arm values are from the posted results table.
efficacy.model: Patient CLL cells with NK effectors (ex-vivo ADCC)
efficacy.note: Inebilizumab plus bendamustine gave ORR 52.8% (2 mg/kg) and 63.9% (4 mg/kg) vs 59.7% for rituximab plus bendamustine.
efficacy.quote: ORR, defined as the proportion of participants with complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) out of total number of participants.
efficacy.reason: ADCC edge over rituximab did not translate
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: the ex-vivo assay (Ward 2011: MEDI-551 'effective at lower mAb doses than rituximab' on primary CLL samples) predicted an advantage over rituximab, and the randomised phase 2 tested exactly that on its primary endpoint; no arm beat rituximab, scored contra with magnitude 'opposite' meaning no gain. Activity per se cannot be separated from bendamustine. Tafasitamab's phase 1 responses (Woyach 2014, 29.6% by CT) were on a secondary measure and do not score.

efficacy.model: CD19 CAR-T in immunodeficient-mouse CD19+ leukemia xenografts
efficacy.note: 4-1BB CD19 CAR-T cured primary ALL xenografts; CLL efficacy was inferred.
efficacy.quote: human T cells expressing anti-CD19 CARs containing CD137 exhibited the greatest antileukemic efficacy and prolonged (>6 months) survival in vivo
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Porter 2011 (CR in one CLL patient) and other early pilots had safety primary endpoints and do not score.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CR/CRi rate vs 5% null, against complete xenograft clearance
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT03331198 first posted 2017-11-06, no results posted. Model side: Sommermeyer 2016 (defined CD4:CD8 CD19 CAR-T in NSG mice), the composition used in liso-cel.
efficacy.model: CD19 CAR-T in immunodeficient-mouse CD19+ leukemia xenografts
efficacy.note: TRANSCEND CLL 004 met its primary endpoint: CR/CRi 18% vs a 5% null in BTKi- and venetoclax-failed patients at 100e6 liso-cel.
efficacy.quote: In the primary efficacy analysis set at DL2 (n=49), the rate of complete response or remission (including with incomplete marrow recovery) was statistically significant at 18% (n=9; 95% CI 9-32; p=0·0006).

patient_trials.quote: At DL2, CR/CRi rate was 45% (95% confidence interval [CI], 31‒60) and overall response rate was 86% (95% CI, 74‒94).

efficacy.reason: Primary CR endpoint met, but low CR
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: the xenograft predicted durable clearance; the trial met its primary endpoint, so same, but 18% CR is far below the mice's complete clearance, so source_calls_it partial. Paired by me (comparison_stated false).

efficacy.model: CAR-T plus concurrent ibrutinib in CLL/ALL xenografts
efficacy.note: Concurrent ibrutinib improved tumor clearance and survival with CTL019 in CLL xenografts.
efficacy.short: Ibrutinib improved CAR-T efficacy in mice
efficacy.quote: Our collective findings indicate that ibrutinib enhances CAR T-cell function and suggest that clinical trials with combination therapy are warranted.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 3-month CR rate on combination, single arm, no monotherapy control
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT02640209 (first posted 2015-12-28) has no posted results. Single arm; no randomised test of the combination exists.
efficacy.model: CAR-T plus concurrent ibrutinib in CLL/ALL xenografts
efficacy.note: Adding huCART-19 to ibrutinib gave a 44% 3-month CR rate in CLL not in CR after ibrutinib; 72% MRD-negative at 12 months.
efficacy.short: CAR-T plus ibrutinib: 44% CR at 3 months
efficacy.quote: While the 3-month CR rate among International Working Group on CLL (iwCLL)-evaluable patients was 44% (90% confidence interval [CI], 23-67%), at 12 months, 72% of patients tested had no measurable residual disease (MRD).

patient_trials.quote: At DL2, CR/CRi rate was 45% (95% confidence interval [CI], 31‒60) and overall response rate was 86% (95% CI, 74‒94).

efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: CR within 3 months was a co-primary endpoint and was high, so same, partial. No randomised comparison exists; Gauthier 2020 found no 1-year PFS difference with vs without ibrutinib (38% vs 50%, P=.91, non-randomised, not primary), which weighs against the model. The liso-cel+ibrutinib cohort (45% CR/CRi vs 18% monotherapy, different population) is listed, not scored.

efficacy.quote: as well as blood and tissue B cells in human CD19/CD20 double transgenic (Tg) mice at lower concentrations than that of the positive control mAb rituximab.
efficacy.note: MEDI-551 out-depleted rituximab in transgenic mice, implying superiority over rituximab in B-cell malignancies including CLL.
efficacy.model: Human CD19/CD20 transgenic mice (MEDI-551 vs rituximab)

efficacy.quote: ORR, defined as the proportion of participants with complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) out of total number of participants.
efficacy.note: Inebilizumab plus bendamustine gave ORR 52.8% (2 mg/kg) and 63.9% (4 mg/kg) vs 59.7% for rituximab plus bendamustine.
efficacy.reason: Mouse edge over rituximab did not translate
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results only (posted 2017-05-31); no journal publication found. Arm values from the posted results table.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: the transgenic mouse ranked MEDI-551 above rituximab; the randomised CLL phase 2 compared exactly that on its primary endpoint and no arm beat rituximab, so contra (magnitude null: no gain, not reversed). Same trial as the draft's ex-vivo ADCC track; mirrors the DLBCL tile's scoring of this mouse.
efficacy.model: Human CD19/CD20 transgenic mice (MEDI-551 vs rituximab)

efficacy.quote: Sustained remission was associated with an elevated frequency of CD27+CD45RO-CD8+ T cells before CAR T cell generation, and these lymphocytes possessed memory-like characteristics.
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo profiling of CLL patients' own T cells and CAR-T products sought determinants of response to CTL019.
efficacy.short: Patient T-cell profile as response predictor
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the system's first use; it was built on the trials' own outcomes.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived T cells and CTL019 products from CLL patients (pre-manufacture CD27+CD45RO-CD8+ phenotype, ex-vivo function)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CR vs non-response by pre-manufacture CD27+CD45RO-CD8+ T-cell frequency
efficacy.quote: Furthermore, a mechanistically relevant population of CD27+PD-1-CD8+ CAR T cells expressing high levels of the IL-6 receptor predicts therapeutic response and is responsible for tumor control.
efficacy.note: T-cell memory phenotype measured before manufacture separated complete responders from non-responders among CTL019-treated CLL patients, after outcomes were known.
efficacy.reason: Built on known outcomes; no prospective test
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Retrospective analysis of CTL019 CLL patients (UPenn pilot NCT01029366, first posted 2009-12-10, and later CLL trials); no prospective patient selection by this phenotype found.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: patient-derived cells used to tell which patients respond are in scope as a patient-level ex_vivo track; because the signature was derived from patients whose response was already known, it is a retrodiction (retro), not same.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived T cells and CTL019 products from CLL patients (pre-manufacture CD27+CD45RO-CD8+ phenotype, ex-vivo function)

safety.confidence_note: Year 2010 is a proxy; data public in the 2020 review.
safety.note: Monkeys showed only on-target B-cell depletion, infusion-time tremor and fever; no infections or cytopenias.
safety.short: Monkeys: B-cell loss, infusion fever only
safety.quote: Importantly, no evidence of an increased susceptibility to infections was noted after tafasitamab administration to cynomolgus monkeys for 13 weeks.

safety.magnitude_basis: infusion-associated reactions in monkeys vs grade 1-2 infusion reactions in CLL
safety.confidence_note: Patient side Woyach 2014 abstract: infusion reactions grade 1-2 most common; grade 3-4 neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia, AST rise, TLS in 5/27.
safety.note: Infusion reactions, foreshadowed by infusion-time fever and tremor in monkeys, were the commonest CLL toxicity; few grade 3-4 cytopenias.
safety.quote: statistically significant differences in body temperature (100-102°F) were observed in males at 100 mg/kg and females at 30 and 100 mg/kg during dosing
safety.judgement: Judgement call: the review's tremor and fever during infusion are read as the model's flag for infusion reactions, which held, so same. Partial because grade 3-4 cytopenias in 5/27 CLL patients were not flagged by monkeys, though marrow infiltration in CLL confounds them; TLS needs tumor the monkeys lacked.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no safety prediction stated in the model papers read.
safety.model: CD19 CAR-T in immunodeficient-mouse CD19+ leukemia xenografts
safety.note: Immunodeficient mice lack the myeloid and cytokine biology for CRS or ICANS, the CAR-T harms seen in CLL patients.
safety.short: Mice cannot show CRS or neurotoxicity
safety.quote: Furthermore, our studies revealed significant discrepancies between in vitro and in vivo surrogate measures of CAR efficacy.
safety.judgement: The xenograft was silent on CRS and neurotoxicity, harms the species could not show, so its silence is not a miss; untested (no_prediction).
